entrypoints.role: A2A AgentCard (Google A2A spec discovery document)
entrypoints.finding: This is the ONLY invocation URL an external A2A peer is told to call. It does NOT mention /api/acp/execute, /api/acp/rpc, or /api/agent/execute at all -- those are a separate, same-origin admin-console tool surface, not part of the documented A2A contract.

entrypoints.role: REAL external A2A peer entrypoint (native + A2A Task format, both tasks/send and tasks/sendSubscribe)
entrypoints.authenticationOwner: session cookie only (`locals.user`, set in hooks.server.ts from `event.cookies.get('auth_session')`) -- NOT Bearer token, despite the AgentCard's documented `authentication.schemes: ['Bearer']`
entrypoints.authorizationOwner: none beyond `if (!locals.user) return 401` at the route level; per-request rate limit (20/user/min via Redis)
entrypoints.dispatchOwner: runGemma4Agent() for the general case; ONE hardcoded exception at line 198-211 (`task.metadata?.skill === 'openspec-workboard'`) that calls executeACPTool('openspec:workboard_recommend', ...) directly from ACPToolRegistry.js

entrypoints.role: Generic ACP tool-dispatch endpoint (admin-console-internal; NOT advertised in agent.json)
entrypoints.authenticationOwner: session cookie only (`if (!locals.user) return 401`) -- no role/permission distinction
entrypoints.authorizationOwner: NONE -- no call to tool-authorization.ts's checkToolAccess()/toolAuthorizationGuard() anywhere in this file
entrypoints.dispatchOwner: executeACPTool(tool, args, {dryRun}) -> `TOOLS[name].handler(args, options)` -- direct call, no intermediate authorization gate

entrypoints.role: LLM tool-calling loop with proper authorization (comparison baseline -- correctly guarded)
entrypoints.finding: This route follows the intended architecture: auth -> capability owner -> dispatch. /api/acp/execute does not.

entrypoints.role: Viterbi-router tool execution endpoint (comparison baseline -- correctly guarded)
entrypoints.finding: tool-authorization.ts's own docstring states: 'Routes that dispatch tools (RPC, agent/execute) must use this module.' This route does; /api/acp/execute does not, despite being architecturally the same kind of route (accepts a caller-supplied tool name + args and dispatches it).

dispatchChain.unguardedPath: peer/caller request -> POST /api/acp/execute -> AUTHENTICATION (locals.user truthy, any role) -> [NO AUTHORIZATION STEP] -> CAPABILITY_RESOLUTION (getACPToolSchema, raw registry lookup) -> DISPATCH (executeACPTool) -> HANDLER (TOOLS[name].handler)
dispatchChain.guardedPath (comparison): peer/caller request -> POST /api/acp/rpc or /api/agent/execute -> AUTHENTICATION (requireAdmin / requireUser) -> AUTHORIZATION (toolAuthorizationGuard -> checkToolAccess against atlasToolRegistry, role-scoped permission set) -> DISPATCH -> HANDLER

boundaryClassification.authentication: present on all 3 execute-style routes (locals.user or requireAdmin/requireUser)
boundaryClassification.discoveryFilter: present only on GET /api/acp/service-ports (A2A-03) and .well-known/agent.json's `skills[]` list -- neither is consulted by POST /api/acp/execute's dispatch path
boundaryClassification.capabilityResolution: getACPToolSchema (ACPToolRegistry.ts, unauthorized) vs atlasToolRegistry lookup inside checkToolAccess (tool-authorization.ts, authorized) -- two SEPARATE registries with two separate tool universes, confirmed live in source (ACPToolRegistry.ts's `TOOLS` object vs atlas-tool-registry.ts's `atlasToolRegistry`)
boundaryClassification.dispatch: direct function call in both cases, no further gate
boundaryClassification.handler: real handlers, several performing genuine Postgres UPDATE/mutation (see suppressedOperations below)

suppressedOperations.mutationClass: UNKNOWN (query is caller-supplied SQL-shaped input; not read further this pass)
FILESYSTEM_WRITE or CANONICAL_WRITE (applies a code fix)
CANONICAL_WRITE (guarded UPDATE kanban_tasks WHERE lane='todo' AND status='pending' AND claimToken IS NULL)
suppressedOperations.dryRunSupported: handled internally via options?.dryRun even though absent from the registry's own DRY_RUN_TOOLS set (a minor doc/set staleness, not a safety gap)

suppressedOperations.mutationClass: EXTERNAL_SIDE_EFFECT, but bounded: action resolves against a fixed enum allowlist (BASH_WORKER_ACTIONS, 6 entries), never a free-text command string -- narrower risk than its name suggests, still unauthorized by role

A single endpoint accepts any string in `tool` and dispatches to whatever ACPToolRegistry.TOOLS[tool] resolves to, entirely independent of what A2A-03 or agent.json chose to advertise.

unknownMethodBehavior: PASS -- unknown/unregistered tool names are rejected with 404 before dispatch (getACPToolSchema check happens before executeACPTool is called). Confirmed both by source read and by the new focused test.

handlerPreventionProof.positiveControl: Unauthenticated request (locals.user = null) -> 401, confirmed by test. Unknown tool name -> 404 before dispatch, confirmed by test.
handlerPreventionProof.negativeControl: Authenticated NON-ADMIN caller ('viewer' role) requesting an unadvertised CANONICAL_WRITE tool ('atlas.kanban.claim') with dryRun:true -> HTTP 200, {success:true, kind:'plan'} -- proves dispatch reached the real handler body. A second test with dryRun omitted (defaults false) against a nonexistent taskId also reaches the real (non-dry-run) code path and returns a clean failure ({success:false, error: string}) rather than being rejected pre-dispatch -- consistent with 'guarded UPDATE matched zero rows', not with any authorization check.
handlerPreventionProof.expectedSafeShape: request -> authentication -> authorization -> REJECT -> dispatch NOT reached -> handler NOT invoked
handlerPreventionProof.actualShape: request -> authentication -> [no authorization step] -> dispatch REACHED -> handler INVOKED
handlerPreventionProof.handlerInvocationCountAssertion: Not measured via a spy/mock call-count (the real handler was exercised directly, safely, via its own dryRun branch, per the file's design) -- the `kind: 'plan'` response value is definitive, non-inferred proof that the handler body executed past its dryRun check, which is only reachable after `TOOLS[name].handler(args, options)` is actually invoked.
handlerPreventionProof.spyBackedAssertion: authorization-boundary.spec.ts, test 5: vi.spyOn(TOOLS["atlas.kanban.claim"], "handler") -- spy.mock.calls.length === 1 for a non-admin caller with no authorization gate. This directly satisfies the requirement that a 401/403/response-shape observation alone is insufficient -- this is a real call-count assertion against the live handler reference.

canonicalAuthorityChecks.evidence: claimKanbanTask() (kanban-task-board.ts:478) performs `UPDATE kanban_tasks SET ... WHERE taskId = $1 AND lane='todo' AND status='pending' AND claimToken IS NULL` -- a caller-supplied taskId that does not match an existing, unclaimed row updates zero rows and the function throws. Peer supply of taskId does not mint or fabricate a task.

canonicalAuthorityChecks.behavior: CALLER_SUPPLIED_ACCEPTED_AS_AUTHORITY (narrower than canonical-identity forgery, but still a real gap)
canonicalAuthorityChecks.evidence: workerId is accepted as-is and becomes the claim's `assignee`; runId/claimToken default to caller-derivable strings if not supplied. This is worker-identity impersonation risk (any authenticated caller can claim a task under an arbitrary workerId string), not canonical-packet/source-identity forgery -- scoped precisely, not overstated.
canonicalAuthorityChecks.rationale: Does not meet the audit's CALLER_SUPPLIED_ACCEPTED_AS_AUTHORITY blocker bar, which is specifically about canonical identity fields (stableFileId, packetKey, sourceRevision, etc.) becoming authoritative merely by being supplied -- none of those fields pass through this tool. Recorded for completeness, not escalated.

canonicalAuthorityChecks.identifier: packetKey / stableFileId / sourceRevision / workspaceRevision / stableSymbolId / symbolVersionId / ContextManifest / ExecutionReceipt references
canonicalAuthorityChecks.evidence: No traced ACP tool in TOOLS accepts any of these fields as direct input this pass (the tool set traced is kanban/db/cache/fix/bash-worker -- none are packet-identity writers). This does not clear the broader packet-identity surface (semantic-packet-writer.ts etc.) for A2A reachability -- that surface was not traced from this route in this pass; it is a distinct question from A2A-04's scope.

mirrorWriteChecks.question: Can a peer invoke A2A-03's suppressed mirror-sync handlers directly even though discovery omits them?
mirrorWriteChecks.answer: Not directly tested this pass for mirror-sync specifically (Qdrant/Neo4j mirror-write tools were not found among the /api/acp/execute TOOLS registry entries traced) -- the concrete finding this pass is about CANONICAL Postgres writes (kanban tasks) via the same unguarded dispatch pattern, which is the same class of risk A2A-03's own text ('Prohibit exposing canonical Postgres/Graphify operations as peer-agent writable state') was written to prevent. The unguarded dispatch pattern itself (/api/acp/execute) is the root cause; any future mirror-sync tool registered in the same TOOLS object would inherit the identical gap.
mirrorWriteChecks.separateGateReport: A2A_PEER_MIRROR_WRITE_EXPOSURE_UNGUARDED applies to the canonical-write case found (kanban tasks); extending this specific trace to mirror-sync (Qdrant/Neo4j) tools specifically was not done this pass and remains open.

existingAuthorizationOwnerReuse.docstringClaim: 'Routes that dispatch tools (RPC, agent/execute) must use this module.'
existingAuthorizationOwnerReuse.recommendation: NOT IMPLEMENTED THIS PASS, per explicit instruction. The fix would be architecturally trivial (wire checkToolAccess/toolAuthorizationGuard into /api/acp/execute the same way /api/agent/execute already does, reusing atlasToolRegistry rather than inventing a parallel permission model) -- but that is a runtime-behavior change, and this task's scope is read-only audit only. Flagged as the fix path for whenever implementation is separately authorized: do NOT introduce a second capability registry or A2A-specific permission model; extend the existing owner.

externalReachabilityCaveat.scope: PRE_FIX_BASELINE; AgentCard authentication-contract discrepancy remains a separate A2A-05 follow-up.
externalReachabilityCaveat.finding: At the time of the baseline audit, the AgentCard (.well-known/agent.json) advertised `authentication.schemes: ['Bearer']`, while hooks.server.ts populated locals.user from a session cookie or DEV_BYPASS_AUTH. This did not mitigate the same-app authorization defect; A2A-04 now adds authorization after authentication.
externalReachabilityCaveat.implication: Bearer/session-cookie parity remains a separate documentation/runtime contract issue. The pre-fix statement that the route had no authorization step is historical and is not the current route behavior; current behavior is recorded under postFix.

resultRationale: The pre-fix audit proved an authenticated viewer could invoke atlas.kanban.claim (handler count 1). The repaired route now checks the existing permission grant and tool-specific required permission before dispatch. The post-fix spy-backed suite proves viewer writes are denied with handler count 0, allowed reads and an admin dry-run still dispatch, unknown tools remain 404, and no durable mutation is performed. See postFix for current evidence; beforeFixResult preserves the historical vulnerability verdict.
